newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS says stepping up cargo flights to Far East.
newsitem.headline: SAS says stepping up cargo flights to Far East.

text.p: Scandinavian airline SAS said on Thursday it would stop operating its Boeing 747-200SF special freighter from Gothenburg, Sweden to New York from August 17 but would step up cargo flights to the Far East.
Since March 1996 the airline has been operating a special freighter version of the Boeing 747 between Gothenburg and Osaka/Macau twice weekly and to New York once a week.
The airline is leased from Atlas Air, painted in SAS colours and flown by SAS pilots. It has a capacity of around 100 tonnes.
"We have decided to swap our cargo capacity to New York and put it in to Macau," Jan Hagen, head of SAS Cargo in Denmark, told Reuters.
The freighter would now fly its usual flights, Gothenburg-Sharjah-Macau-Osaka, on Wednesdays and Fridays in addition to the new Gothenburg-Sharjah-Macau flight on Sundays, Hagen said.
"The reason for doing that is there is not demand for capacity into Japan but we see lots of demand to Macau."
The airline's new five times weekly passenger flights with a Boeing 767 to New York would compensate for the loss of cargo capacity to the U.S. east coast, Hagen said.
The re-routing would also allow an opportunity to swap pallets with its partner Lufthansa Cargo AG at the German carrier's Sharjah hub, Hagen said.
SAS is patrly owned by the governments of Sweden, Denmark and Norway.
